          September 2026 Article 405 Deviation Reporting

Dear Secretary Reese,

Kleinschmidt Associates, on behalf of Relevate Power (Relevate) and C-S Canal Hydro LLC,
owner and licensee, respectively, for the Waterloo and Seneca Falls Project (FERC No. 2438)
on the Seneca River in New York, is filing this Article 405 Deviation Report for the month of
September 2026.

September 2026 Article 405 Reporting

During the month of September 2026, the level of Seneca Lake was below the target elevation.
The precipitation received for the month of September has been approximately 25% of the
normal precipitation rate. Lower water levels are typical for this time of year depending on
precipitation, and are consistent with this time in 2025, 2022, 2020, and 2016.

Throughout the month of September 2026 the level of the Cayuga-Seneca Canal has been in
compliance with the requirement to be maintained no lower than 0.5 ft below the Seneca
Lake elevation.

Throughout September 2026, the level of Van Cleef Lake was maintained within the target
elevation range as established in the Order Granting Temporary License Variance dated
November 12, 2025, and extended to October 22, 2026 by Order dated May 1, 2026 1.

 REGULATORY             BACKGROUND LICENSE ARTICLE: ART405: The licensee shall operate the Waterloo and Seneca Falls
 REQUIREMENTS:          Project to control fluctuations of the reservoir surface elevation at each development for the protection of
                        wetlands, wildlife, and fish habitat and recreational opportunities in the project impoundments. The
                        licensee shall act at all times to maintain the impoundment water surface elevations, as measured at the
                        agreed upon gage location, as follows:

                        Maintain the Seneca Lake impoundment within ±0.3 foot of the seasonal target elevations of 446.0 feet
                        BCD during the summer and 445.0 feet BCD during the winter. During flood control events the
                        impoundment upper limit is +0.55 foot. The elevation of Seneca Lake is subordinate to the
                        maintenance of the water levels for navigation and minimum flow to sustain Van Cleef Lake
                        elevations. As excepted below when Seneca Lake levels drop below 445.9 feet BCD summer and 444.9
                        feet BCD winter, the Seneca Falls Powerhouse will be placed in a no discharge non-power generation
                        status. The Waterloo powerhouse will operate to discharge flows required to maintain the navigation
                        levels and minimum flow for Van Cleef Lake.

                        The Seneca Lake transition from winter to summer takes place in a 20-day period beginning March 1 and
                        a transition from summer to winter in a 45-day period beginning November 1. For the transition periods
                        the target increments of daily change in elevation are: summer +0.053 foot and winter -0.023 foot. The
                        transitions are conditioned on any surplus or deficiency of precipitation.

                        Maintain Van Cleef Lake impoundment at a target elevation of 430.5 feet BCD with a maximum daily
                        water level fluctuation of ±0.25 foot. During the non-navigation season (December 1 to April 30), when so
                        requested by local authorities and after consultation with the New York State Canal Corporation (NYSCC)
                        Van Cleef Lake may be drawn down to an absolute minimum of 425.5 feet BCD by the operation of the

               Seneca Falls powerhouse to aid local flood control. As needed, the Seneca Falls powerhouse will operate
               due to local runoff to control the navigation level of Van Cleef Lake.

               The Waterloo development maintains the Cayuga-Seneca Canal portion of the Waterloo impoundment as
               measured in close proximity to the powerhouse, at the location described in the approved flow
               monitoring plan required by section B.6 of the modified Water Quality Certification, such that the surface
               water elevation does not fluctuate more than 0.5 foot below the daily average surface elevation as
               measured at the NYSCC Geneva gage on Seneca Lake. The daily average surface elevation to be used is
               the average elevation of the previous calendar day at the Geneva gage.

               The licensee may vary from the recommended water level management regime for Seneca Lake, the
               Seneca Canal portion at the Waterloo Impoundment, and/or for Van Cleef Lake due to circumstances
               beyond the control of the licensee (flood control or emergency conditions) and for short periods of time
               upon mutual agreement with the NYSCC, with notification to the New York State Department of
               Environmental Conservation Regional Permit Administrator within 5 days. If the water level management
               regime for Seneca Lake, the Waterloo impoundment, and/or Van Cleef Lake is so modified, the licensee
               shall notify the Commission as soon as possible, but not later than 10 calendar days after the end of the
               month in which each incident occurred.
EVENT              • The elevation of Seneca Lake was below target during September 2026 due to abnormally low
DESCRIPTION             precipitation in the region. Required environmental flows were maintained throughout the

                        established in the Order Granting Temporary License Variance dated November 12, 2025, and
                        extended to October 22, 2026 by Order Granting Extension of Temporary Variance of Article 405
                        dated May 1, 2026 (Accession Number 20260501-3009).

Good afternoon,

I am writing to inform you that the elevation of Seneca Falls Lake has continued to drop to a low elevation of approximately 445.2 ft.
Average inflows to the Cayuga-Seneca Canal have been approximately 300 cfs for the last 30 days. These lower water levels currently
being experienced at Seneca Falls Lake (below target levels) do typically occur during the summer period depending on precipitation.
The low levels currently being experienced are consistent with those experienced last year and in 2022 (see attached), as well as in
2020 and 2016. Precipitation in the vicinity of the Project is less than half of normal for the last 30 days or so (see attached).

The FERC License and Water Quality Certification for the Project requires Seneca Falls Lake to be maintained within 0.3 ft of 446.0 ft in
the summer. However, the elevation of Seneca Lake is subordinate to the maintenance of the water levels for navigation (Cayuga-
Seneca canal) and the minimum flow to sustain Van Cleef Lake, which is currently being maintained approximately 2 ft lower than its
minimum summer elevation of 430.25 ft as per the Article 405 temporary variance to address shoreline remediation needs.

The Cayuga-Seneca Canal has been in compliance with the requirement to be maintained no more than 0.5 ft lower than the Seneca
Falls Lake elevation during this time. The Seneca Falls powerhouse is off-line and has been for most of the summer. Flows of
approximately 175 cfs are currently discharged through Gate 4, which would otherwise be passed at the spillway, as well as the lock
system. The Waterloo powerhouse is intermittently operational to maintain elevations in Seneca Falls Lake and the Cayuga-Seneca
Canal, as well as provide flows needed to retain the elevation in Van Cleef Lake, and meet the required minimum flows of 100 cfs from
June through September.

Please let us know if you have any questions.

Thank you,

Kelly Maloney
GM, Relevate Power Portfolio

Subject: Seneca Falls Notification

Good morning,

I am writing to inform you that the elevation of Seneca Falls Lake has been variable at the low elevation of 445.7 ft for approximately the
last 14 days and has been steadily below elevation 445.7 ft (at 445.6 ft) for approximately the last week. These lower water levels
currently being experienced at Seneca Falls Lake (below target levels) do typically occur during the summer period depending on
precipitation.

The FERC License and Water Quality Certification for the Project requires Seneca Falls Lake to be maintained within 0.3 ft of 446.0 ft in
the summer. However, the elevation of Seneca Lake is subordinate to the maintenance of the water levels for navigation (Cayuga-
Seneca canal) and the minimum flow to sustain Van Cleef Lake, which is currently being maintained approximately 2 ft lower than its
minimum summer elevation of 430.25 ft as per the Article 405 temporary variance to address shoreline remediation needs. The
Cayuga-Seneca Canal has been in compliance with the requirement to be maintained no more than 0.5 ft lower than the Seneca Falls
Lake elevation during this time. The Seneca Falls powerhouse is off-line and the Waterloo powerhouse is intermittently operational to
maintain elevations in Seneca Falls Lake and the Cayuga-Seneca Canal, as well as provide flows needed to retain the elevation in Van
Cleef Lake.

Please let us know if you have any questions.

Thank you,
